title: Composing operations
objectives: Translate a temporal sequence into the correct matrix product.
Show a noncommuting pair and distinguish it from associativity.
Prove that a compatible product of stochastic matrices is stochastic.

quizzes.question: A acts first, then B, on a column probability vector p. Which expression describes the result?
feedback: ABp applies B to p first; it reverses the stated sequence.
Correct. The intermediate state is Ap, so the second action is B(Ap).
A temporal composition is matrix multiplication, not addition.

quizzes.question: Identity and flip agree on the uniform bit distribution. Are they therefore the same operation?
options: Yes: one matching output proves equality.
No: they disagree on a definite basis input.
They agree on every other input too.
feedback: One input is not enough to establish equality of linear maps.
Correct. On |0⟩, identity outputs |0⟩ while flip outputs |1⟩.
They agree on the uniform vector, but not on the basis inputs.

source: Lecture Slides - 1 to 7.pdf, PDF pp.12–13. The multiplication refresher, closure proof, commuting example and state-sufficiency discussion provide expanded lecture-note exposition.
prerequisites: Basic arithmetic and elementary algebra. A matrix-multiplication refresher is included before composition.
